84.bio: Mary Shelley was an English novelist who brought Gothic storytelling into conversation with scientific ambition and human responsibility. Frankenstein grew out of a ghost-story challenge in 1816. She also wrote The Last Man, imagining a future transformed by catastrophe.

11.bio: Lewis Carroll was the pen name of Charles Lutwidge Dodgson, an English mathematician, writer and photographer. Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland and Through the Looking-Glass turn logic and language into imaginative play. His nonsense verse includes The Hunting of the Snark and Jabberwocky.

1952.bio: Charlotte Perkins Gilman was an American writer and social critic concerned with women’s independence and the conditions shaping everyday life. 12242.bio: Emily Dickinson was an American poet who spent most of her life in Amherst, Massachusetts. Her compact poems explore nature, death, belief and inner experience through striking imagery and unconventional rhythms. Much of her poetry appeared after her death; early editors changed some wording and punctuation.
12242.edition: Historical editions edited by Mabel Loomis Todd and Thomas Wentworth Higginson (credits vary by series and are retained in the PDF). All three series in this collection, not every poem Dickinson ever wrote. Early editorial conventions are preserved. Source cover supplied by Project Gutenberg.

21.bio: Aesop is the traditional name attached to a body of ancient fables, often featuring animals whose choices reveal human strengths and weaknesses. 2701.bio: Herman Melville was an American writer of the American Renaissance period. Among his best-known works are Moby-Dick (1851), Typee (1846), a romanticized account of his experiences in Polynesia, and Billy Budd, Sailor, a posthumously published novella. At the time of his death, Melville was not well known to the public, but 1919, the centennial of his birth, was the starting point of a Melville revival.

2554.bio: Fyodor Mikhailovich Dostoevsky was a Russian philosopher, novelist, short-story writer, essayist, and journalist. He is regarded as one of the greatest novelists in both Russian and world literature, and many of his works are considered highly influential masterpieces. Dostoevsky's literary works explore the human condition in the troubled political, social and spiritual atmospheres of 19th-century Russia, and engage with a variety of philosophical and religious themes.

203.bio: Harriet Elisabeth Beecher Stowe was an American author and abolitionist. She came from the Beecher family and wrote a popular novel called Uncle Tom's Cabin (1852), which depicts the harsh conditions experienced by enslaved African Americans. 6130.bio: Homer was an ancient Greek poet who is traditionally credited as the author of the Iliad and the Odyssey, two epic poems that are foundational works of ancient Greek literature. Homer was highly revered in ancient Greek society and is considered one of the most influential authors in history. The question of Homer's identity and existence—dubbed the "Homeric Question"—continues to be debated, and scholars generally regard the two poems as the works of separate authors.
